officialTitle: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan after Endocrine Therapy in Metastatic Breast Cancer
setting: Metastatic, after one or more lines of endocrine-based therapy and no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of the 866 patients who underwent randomization, 713 had HER2-low disease, and 153 had HER2-ultralow disease.
design.notes: 1:1 randomisation. HER2-low: IHC 1+ or 2+ with negative ISH; HER2-ultralow: IHC 0 with membrane staining (exploratory population).

clinicalQuestion: Does trastuzumab deruxtecan improve PFS over physician's choice chemotherapy in chemotherapy-naive HR-positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer after endocrine-based therapy?

pico.population: HR-positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer after one or more lines of endocrine-based therapy, no previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by BICR in HER2-low population. Secondary: PFS in all randomised patients, OS, safety

publications.title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan after Endocrine Therapy in Metastatic Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Among the patients with HER2-low disease, the median progression-free survival was 13.2 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 11.4 to 15.2) in the trastuzumab deruxtecan group and 8.1 months (95% CI, 7.0 to 9.0) in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.75; P<0.001); the results were consistent in the exploratory HER2-ultralow population. Data for overall survival were immature.

safety.description: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 52.8% of the patients in the trastuzumab deruxtecan group and in 44.4% of those in the chemotherapy group.

safety.description: Adjudicated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis (three grade 5 events with trastuzumab deruxtecan)
safety.sourceQuote: Adjudicated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 49 patients (11.3%; three events were grade 5 in severity) and in 1 patient (0.2%; grade 2), respectively.

strengths: Large randomised phase III trial with PFS by blinded independent central review
Moved the HER2-low question into the chemotherapy-naive, post-endocrine setting and explored HER2-ultralow disease
limitations: Higher rate of grade 3 or higher adverse events than chemotherapy, including fatal ILD

clinicalImplications.text: Supports trastuzumab deruxtecan as an option before conventional chemotherapy for HR-positive, HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after endocrine-based therapy; HER2-ultralow data are exploratory.

tumourBoardPearl.text: For HR+/HER2-low disease progressing on endocrine-based therapy, T-DXd can be considered ahead of first chemotherapy — but OS was immature at primary analysis.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 39282896.
